description: Hi! We're Orbital Vitals, a team from Sydney building HALO, a health copilot for astronauts on Moon and Mars missions. It learns each astronaut's own baseline, flags meaningful changes early, and gives clear offline guidance when Earth is too far to answer in time, grounded in NASA space-medicine research and real NASA solar-storm data. We'd love a UX/UI designer, data/ML person, and health advisor. All levels are welcome. We'll plan before the event. Message us; we'd love to hear from you!
summary: HALO (Health Autonomy Loop for Orbit) is an on-board health copilot for astronauts on long missions, built for the moments when Earth is too far away to answer in time. On the way to Mars, a signal takes up to about 20 minutes each way, so a question to the flight surgeon can take 40. HALO closes the care loop on the spacecraft itself, fully offline. It learns each astronaut's own pre-flight baseline and flags drift in sleep, heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, glucose, mood, exercise and reaction time before it becomes an emergency. Every reading is also checked against published clinical guidelines (AHA, CDC, ADA, AASM), and every flag is linked to NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight. When the delay is long, HALO switches to autonomous mode: deterministic, explainable triage that uses only what is in the medical kit, read aloud step by step, with a flight-surgeon packet queued for downlink. The dashboard has 18 screens, including a 3D body map, camera and Bluetooth heart-rate sensors, a radiation dose ledger with a 3D storm shelter, EVA and landing readiness, and a Mars-sol sleep planner. It runs on real NASA data: DONKI solar storms (live API plus 352 bundled events), NASA-STD-3001 limits and Curiosity radiation measurements. In 500 simulated healthy missions, HALO raised 2 false alarms versus 54 for a fixed rule. Earth Mode reuses the same engine in Antarctic stations and remote clinics on Earth. Crew data is simulated; HALO is a prototype, not a medical device.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
HALO (Health Autonomy Loop for Orbit) is an on-board health copilot for astronauts on long missions. On the way to Mars, a signal takes up to about 20 minutes each way, so the crew cannot wait for Earth in an emergency. HALO runs fully offline on the spacecraft and closes the care loop in four steps:

  1. Measure: one-tap logs, a contact-free camera pulse reading, any Bluetooth heart-rate strap, and short tests (NASA's 3-minute Reaction Self-Test protocol, a near-vision check, a balance check and the PHQ-2 mood screen).
  2. Compare: every reading goes through two lenses. Personal drift compares it with the astronaut's own pre-flight baseline (robust median and spread, persistence and hysteresis to avoid false alarms). Published clinical guidelines (AHA, NHLBI, CDC, ADA, AASM) say when a value is abnormal for anyone.
  3. Decide: a deterministic, explainable rule tree gives self-manage, monitor or urgent. Every decision shows its reason and its source.
  4. Act and report: when the one-way delay is 5 minutes or more, HALO runs the protocol first. It reads the steps aloud, uses only what is in the on-board medical kit, and queues a one-page flight-surgeon packet for downlink.

HOW IT WORKS (THE DASHBOARD)
The dashboard has 18 screens in four sections.

  • Monitor: Mission Console with a crew health index; a 3D body map of 7 body systems; Log & Measure; Sensors & Validation (camera pulse using the POS method, Bluetooth strap with heart-rate variability, and Bland–Altman agreement); Drift & 7-day Forecast with what-if countermeasures; Radiation & Space Weather with a 3D Earth-to-Mars transfer, a dose ledger and a 3D storm-shelter cutaway.
  • Act: Autonomous Triage; EVA Go/No-Go and Landing Readiness; a Mars-sol sleep and light planner (24 h 39 min 35 s day); a Ground Link that obeys the real light-time delay; the Flight Surgeon Packet; and Crew Pulse, a team view with consent-based privacy.
  • Evidence: Clinical Reference with every threshold cited; a Simulation Lab that runs 1,000 seeded missions; a tamper-evident Health Black Box (SHA-256 hash chain); and Science & Sources, where every number links to its source.
  • Impact: Earth Mode re-labels the same engine for Antarctic stations, remote and outback clinics, and home care. A 60-second Mars transit story shows it all: sleep drift caught on day 51, the real 20 May 2024 solar storm on day 90, and a fever handled autonomously on day 157.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

  • Earlier warning: in the simulation, personal baselines caught declines that a fixed rule missed in naturally long sleepers. They also raised 2 false alarms in 500 healthy missions, against 54 for the fixed rule.
  • Crew autonomy: clear, spoken steps when Earth cannot answer in time, with a record ready for the surgeon.
  • Trust: no black box. Every rule, threshold and number is visible and sourced.
  • Reach on Earth: the same approach helps anywhere specialists are far away.

NASA DATA AND SCIENCE

  • NASA CCMC DONKI: 352 real space-weather events (181 flares, 144 CMEs, 27 SEP events) bundled for offline use, plus a live API client with a NASA backup endpoint, retries, and validation.
  • NASA-STD-3001 radiation limits and Curiosity RAD dose measurements.
  • NASA Human Research Program's five hazards and human-system risks.
  • NASA's Reaction Self-Test and the NASA-funded ISS sleep research.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY
TypeScript, React, Vite and Tailwind CSS; Recharts and three.js for charts and 3D; Framer Motion; Web Bluetooth (GATT Heart Rate service), camera (getUserMedia), Web Speech for read-aloud and voice commands; a service worker and manifest for an installable offline app. Testing uses Vitest (73 unit tests), Playwright (128 end-to-end checks, plus a sensor test bench and a layout audit) and axe-core (0 accessibility violations). The code is open source on GitHub, and the app also ships as a single offline HTML file.

CREATIVITY HALO judges each astronaut against their own normal rather than a population average. It ties every flag to NASA's hazard model and degrades gracefully as the communication delay grows. It also brings a contact-free camera pulse reading, a hologram body map and a 3D storm shelter into a tool built for gloved hands, with large targets, high contrast and read-aloud.

FACTORS CONSIDERED
Safety and honesty come first: the crew data is simulated, and HALO is a prototype decision-support tool, not a medical device. Triage steps would need flight-surgeon review, and every threshold cites its source. We also designed for offline reliability, explainability, crew privacy and accessibility (glove mode, high contrast, reduced motion, screen readers). The next step is validation on NASA analog mission data such as HERA and CHAPEA.
